title: Cross-View PSD Distillation for Viewpoint-Robust Remote Photoplethysmography

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to make rPPG heart-rate estimation robust to non-frontal camera viewpoints. None of the prior papers explicitly address this purpose. Papers [1], [2], [3], [5], [6], [7], [9], [12], [14], [20], and [17] discuss rPPG heart-rate estimation but focus on different challenges, such as robustness to environmental noise, video quality, or alternative body regions (e.g., neck, arms, or legs). None of these papers target robustness to non-frontal viewpoints specifically.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves asymmetric cross-view PSD distillation, transferring frequency-domain (power spectral density) knowledge from a reliable frontal view to side views during training, exploiting the view-invariance of the cardiac PSD. Papers [13], [16], [19], [21], [22], [27], and [28] discuss knowledge distillation techniques, including cross-view and frequency-domain distillation. Paper [16] introduces "view alignment" for knowledge distillation, and paper [21] explores frequency-domain representations for distillation. While these papers address distillation in general, none specifically apply it to rPPG or cardiac PSD transfer across camera viewpoints. Paper [25] discusses view-invariant representations but focuses on action recognition, not rPPG. Thus, no prior paper contains a substantively equivalent mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses the MCD-rPPG dataset to measure heart rate estimation accuracy (MAE reduction) and the frontal-to-side gap. Papers [1], [3], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], [12], [14], [17], and [20] evaluate rPPG methods using similar metrics (e.g., MAE, accuracy) and datasets. For example, paper [8] uses a 10-minute video dataset with ECG ground truth, and paper [12] benchmarks rPPG algorithms on the MR-NIRP Car dataset. These papers share the same evaluation design (benchmark-based validation with MAE or accuracy metrics), even though the specific dataset (MCD-rPPG) differs. Therefore, the evaluation facet is covered.

### Domain
The domain is remote photoplethysmography (rPPG). Many prior papers ([1], [2], [3], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10], [12], [14], [17], [20]) work in the rPPG domain, addressing heart rate estimation and related challenges. Although this contribution targets a specific sub-problem (non-frontal viewpoints), the general application area (rPPG) is well-covered.
